changelog: Paraphrased C8 to shorten its wording and free space for one new principle.

Inserted a new core principle after C8 that addresses the primary finding: avoid trading a single high-contradiction cut for adjacent splits that fragment NPs/enumerations, and prefer cuts that preserve noun/list integrity and keep predicates with their core arguments.

Inserted a new Core Principle after C5 requiring that verbs/predicates stay with their core arguments/complements and that cuts be delayed until the verb phrase and obligatory complements are present — to address the primary finding about predicate completion.
Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_956 (≤3) to teach the scorer about short-latency NP/list fragmentation errors identified in the primary finding.
Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_1253 (≤3) to show how adjacent cuts can fragment coordinated NPs/enumerations and encourage preserving list integrity.
Replace E3 with labeled example en_us_1113 (≤5) to demonstrate predicate-completion failures where cuts separate verbs from their core arguments.
Replace E4 with labeled example en_us_1280 (≤3) to illustrate long NP fragmentation in very short-latency scenarios and discourage trading one high-contra cut for many smaller fragments.

Replace C6 with a concise 'Predicate completion' principle to address the primary finding: avoid cutting verbs/predicates from their core arguments or complements and delay cuts until the verb phrase and required objects are present.
